data.title: Gryphon Capital Income Trust Reports Unit Purchase Plan Results
data.description:

data.title: Café de Coral Revenue Falls 1%; Interim Profit Rises 116.7%
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Cafe de Coral Holdings Ltd. ( (HK:0341) ).

Café de Coral Holdings, a restaurant group with fast-food, casual-dining and institutional-catering businesses in Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland, reported first-half FY2026/27 revenue of HK$3,995.2 million, down 1.0%, while profit attributable to shareholders rose 116.7% to HK$101.3 million. The company said performance and profitability improved across business units through growth initiatives, operating-model optimisation, store-network rationalisation and cost-efficiency measures amid changing consumption patterns, budget-conscious spending and competition.

Fast-food operations combined value offers, product innovation, customer segmentation and AI-powered Club 100 analytics; quality and service procedures were used to drive repeat patronage. Chinese Mainland sales and profit improved through O2O sales, network optimisation and an asset-light model, while prudent expansion deepened the Greater Bay Area presence.

Casual Dining and Institutional Catering made greater contributions through same-store sales growth, improved profitability and market-share gains. The company declared a HK15-cent interim dividend, up from HK10 cents, with an 84.5% payout ratio.

data.title: Ero Copper Temporarily Suspends Tucumã Production Activities
data.description:
An announcement from Ero Copper ( (TSE:ERO) ) is now available.

SEMAS directed Ero to temporarily suspend mining at Tucumã after intense rainfall caused two localized contact-water overflow events. The company then suspended all mining and processing activities, while adding pumping and storage resources and relocating a stockpile after notifying the regulator.

SEMAS said its assessment found anomalous pH readings in local water samples, and requested a final remediation plan for review while dialogue with Ero remains ongoing. Fines tied to the overflows totalled approximately US$2.9 million, while Ero said it had not received documentation supporting a separate US$1.9 million fish-mortality fine and that it had identified no correlation with Tucumã.
